definitions.explanation: The act of stopping or restraining someone from doing something, typically by physical intervention or verbal command. Often used when preventing someone from acting rashly or dangerously.

examples.japanese: {周|まわ}りの{人|ひと}が{制止|せいし}した。
examples.english: The people around held him back.

examples.japanese: {警備員|けいびいん}の{制止|せいし}を{振|ふ}り{切|き}って{走|はし}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: He broke free from the security guard's restraint and ran out.

examples.japanese: {友人|ゆうじん}の{制止|せいし}も{聞|き}かず、{彼|かれ}は{危険|きけん}な{場所|ばしょ}に{向|む}かった。
examples.english: Ignoring his friend's attempts to stop him, he headed for the dangerous area.

notes:
Often appears in news and literary contexts describing scenes where someone is being physically or verbally restrained.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{制止|せいし}する (to restrain, to stop someone)
・{制止|せいし}を{振|ふ}り{切|き}る (to shake off restraint)
・{制止|せいし}を{無視|むし}する (to ignore attempts to stop one)
・{制止|せいし}も{聞|き}かず (ignoring attempts to stop one)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{制止|せいし} — stopping someone from acting (physical/verbal intervention)
・{抑制|よくせい} — suppression, restraint (broader; includes self-restraint and systemic controls)
